untouched_lookback.note: Full 20-300 range only for the base experiment (sl 3/4/5, ratio 2.5-6.0). All boundary-extension coverage (sl=6 full ratio range, and ratio 6.5-8.0 for any sl) is restricted to lookback 20-160 -- prior broad sweep showed the useful structural region concentrates at lower lookback, so the extension intentionally does not re-sweep 170-300.

sl_atr_multiplier.note: 3/4/5 cover the full base rectangle (width 3-14 x lookback 20-300 x ratio 2.5-6.0). 6 exists ONLY over the boundary-extension coverage (lookback 20-160, ratio 2.5-6.0), see coverage_geometry below.

tp_sl_ratio.note: 2.5-6.0 covers the full base rectangle for sl in {3,4,5} (lookback 20-300) and, for sl=6, the boundary-extension subset (lookback 20-160). 6.5-8.0 exists ONLY over the boundary-extension coverage (lookback 20-160) for sl in {3,4,5,6}. This is NOT a full width x lookback x sl x ratio Cartesian rectangle -- see coverage_geometry.

execution.descriptive_seconds_per_candidate_note: Average over the whole batch, not a marginal cost -- semantic computation reuse inside one EvaluationContext; not directly comparable to the 3D experiment's 2.21s/candidate average since batch composition/size differ.

notes: Executed as a single 8352-candidate range-batch (lab_ema500_4d_stop_x_ratio), one Strategy Engine process, one EvaluationContext -- no width/lookback/stop-loss/ratio chunking. sources.json lists the single source batch_id. This is the largest single physical run in the BBB research evidence repo to date; also serves as a single-process performance baseline for this candidate set/scale.

history.note: Right-boundary shape probe on two exit dimensions: new SL=6 over ratio 2.5-6.0, and ratio continuation 6.5-8.0 for SL in {3,4,5,6}. Both restricted to lookback 20-160 (not a lookback re-sweep) and width 3-14, per instruction -- prior broad sweep showed the useful structural region concentrates at lower lookback. TP computed via the same canonical ratio semantics (TP=SL*ratio). Original attempt as a single 4320-candidate range-batch was OOM-killed by the Docker Desktop VM's 8.32GB memory ceiling at 832/4320 candidates (strategy-engine RSS climbing past 6.6GB and still rising, exit code 137, OOMKilled=true) -- those 832 already-computed candidates were salvaged (their per-candidate summary metrics reconstructed from raw trades.json using the exact same formula as the batch orchestrator, verified byte-identical against a known official candidate summary before use) and NOT recomputed. The remaining 3488 were split into 5 coarse chunks along natural SL boundaries (608 + 720x4), each executed as its own single range-batch, one Strategy Engine process, sequential (no parallel workers), well below the OOM threshold observed. 4320/4320 completed across the salvage + 5 chunks, 0 failed, 0 duplicates, 0 missing planned identities, 0 overlap with the existing 8352-row base coverage. 6 distinct market_data_hash values (one per physical run attempt, each resolving the live 'full_available' window at a different wall-clock time) -- not a single shared hash across this stage, unlike single-range-batch experiments.
